title: Halloween events planned throughout October in St. Joseph and Southwest Michigan

Halloween events planned throughout October in St. Joseph and Southwest Michigan
St. Joseph Today has announced a lineup of Halloween events throughout October in St. Joseph and Southwest Michigan. Activities include a scavenger hunt, pumpkin displays, a costume parade, and trick-or-treating. The events are open to families and community members.
St. Joseph Today has announced a series of Halloween-themed events taking place throughout October in St. Joseph and Southwest Michigan. The festivities are designed for families and community members, offering a range of activities leading up to Halloween.
From October 1 to 31, the 'Where's the Witch' scavenger hunt invites participants to find a hidden witch in 13 participating downtown St. Joseph locations. Passports for the hunt can be picked up at the St. Joe Today Welcome Center, and completed passports can be returned for a prize.
On Saturday, October 17, Downtown Spooktacular will return to downtown St. Joseph. The free event will be held in Lake Bluff Park, Whirlpool Centennial Park, and the North Pier St. Joseph Lighthouse in Tiscornia Park. Activities will include a Spooktacular Market, a costume parade, spooky lighthouse tours, a pumpkin carving display and demonstration, hayrides through downtown, magic shows, a pumpkin patch and decorating station, a hay maze, and a spooky trolley.
From October 19 to 31, local businesses and restaurants across Southwest Michigan will participate in Pumpkins on Parade, displaying decorated pumpkins for the public to view and vote for their favorites.
The month concludes with a classic Halloween Trick-Or-Treat event on Friday, October 30, from 4:30 p.m. to 6 p.m. in downtown St. Joseph and the Benton Harbor Arts District. Merchants will welcome costumed trick-or-treaters during this festive event.
"St. Joe Today is a 501(c)(3) membership-based organization dedicated to developing and promoting events and happenings in St. Joseph, Michigan and its surrounding communities," according to St. Joseph Today.
